title: Imperatives, suggestions and offers
tagline: Giving instructions, making suggestions, and offering — politely.
exam: Speaking Part 2 — making a decision together
why: Signs, notices and short messages in Reading Part 1 are full of imperatives (Don't touch, Keep off the grass), and Speaking Part 2 asks you to make suggestions and reach a decision with a partner — the exact job of Let's…, Shall we…? and How about…?

hook.text: Miss Vega claps her hands. "Open your books, please. Don't forget your pencils!" Later, Sofia whispers: "Let's sit together — shall we ask Miss Vega first?"
hook.ask: Miss Vega gives instructions, and Sofia makes a suggestion. Which words does each of them use to start?

diagrams.title: Instruction, negative, or suggestion?

let's + base verb, a suggestion for you and me

diagrams.caption: Imperatives jump straight to the verb. Suggestions add a little phrase (let's, shall we, why don't we) first.

diagrams.title: How to accept or refuse politely

steps.label: Give a short, polite reason if you refuse

diagrams.caption: A polite answer is quick — react, decide, and give a reason only if you say no.

head: Function
Structure
Example
rows: Shall we / Why don't we + base verb?

examples.note: base verb, no subject — a classroom instruction
be also works as an imperative

examples.text: Take your shoes off at the door.
examples.note: a house rule or a sign

use.point: Suggestions: let's, shall we, why don't we, how about

examples.text: Let's go to the park this afternoon.
examples.note: let's + base verb, for you and me
shall we + base verb, a friendly question

examples.text: Why don't we ask Miss Vega for help?

examples.note: would you like + noun or to + base verb

examples.text: I'd love to, but I've got homework.

watch_out.why: Imperatives don't use a subject (you) — just the base verb.
The negative imperative needs don't, not just not.

watch_out.wrong: Let's to go to the park.
watch_out.why: Let's is followed by the base verb, with no to.
How about is followed by -ing, not the base verb.

watch_out.wrong: Would you like coming with us?
watch_out.right: Would you like to come with us?
watch_out.why: Would you like + to + base verb (or a noun), not -ing.

l1.why: English imperatives never use a subject pronoun, even though Spanish sometimes implies tú.

l1.right: Shall we go to the park? / Let's go to the park.
l1.why: A Spanish question with vamos needs a real suggestion structure in English, not just a statement with a question mark.

l1.wrong: What about if we go swimming?
l1.why: How about is followed directly by -ing, with no if.

l1.wrong: I would love, but I have homework.
l1.right: I'd love to, but I've got homework.
l1.why: Love needs to after it here (I'd love to), and got often follows have in British English.
The English negative imperative always uses don't, not no.

remember.trick: DON'T + verb to stop it, LET'S + verb to start it!
remember.tip: An imperative has no subject — it jumps straight to the verb. A suggestion usually needs let's, shall we or how about first.

dialogue.title: Planning Nadia's surprise
dialogue.context: Sofia, Mateo and Liam plan a surprise party for Nadia after school, with Miss Vega's help.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: Don't worry, my lips are sealed. Let's decorate the classroom.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Good idea! Mateo, bring some balloons tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Mateo
lines.text: OK. How about bringing a cake as well?

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: Would you like some help from me?

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Yes, please! Why don't we ask you to keep Nadia busy at three o'clock?

lines.speaker: Miss Vega
lines.text: I'd love to. Now — don't forget to keep it a secret!

can_do: I can give instructions and warnings with imperatives and don't + verb.
I can make suggestions with Let's…, Shall we…?, Why don't we…? and How about + -ing?
I can accept or politely refuse an offer or a suggestion.
summary: Imperatives use the base verb with no subject: Close the door. Be quiet.
Negative imperatives use don't + base verb: Don't run.
Suggest with Let's, Shall we…?, Why don't we…? and How about + -ing?
Offer with Would you like…? + a noun or to + base verb.
Accept warmly (Let's do it!) or refuse politely, with a short reason.
